# Pixtral vision reference fixtures

What the Rust Pixtral image preprocessing and prompt layout must reproduce,
generated by Hugging Face's own processor on OpenVINO/pixtral-12b-int4-ov
(`tools/vlm_fixtures/gen_pixtral_fixtures.py --run-ir`, transformers 5.14.1,
Pillow 12.3; versions are recorded in the JSON):

- `*.png`: the same eight synthetic images as the Gemma 4 fixtures.
- `reference.json`:
  - `processor`: longest edge 1024, patch 16, bicubic, CLIP mean/std.
  - `tokens`: `[IMG]`, `[IMG_BREAK]`, `[IMG_END]` ids.
  - `images.<name>`: resized size, patch grid and a summary of `pixel_values`
    for the torchvision (`fast`) and PIL (`slow`) processors.
  - `prompts.<name>`: the rendered template (one `[IMG]` per image), the
    processor's `input_ids`, the image names and grids.
  - `vision_ir`: the vision IR's rows for two images.

The two processors agree on every size and grid; their pixels differ (up to
0.015, and 0.30 on the 3x1200 image), so the Rust port is held bit-identical
to the PIL processor only. Pillow 12 resizes an image more than 100 times
taller than wide in two calls (height first), which the shared resampler
mirrors; `pole_3x1200` exercises it.
